description:
Companion software artefact for the manuscript SARAI: Sovereignty-Aware Risk Assessment Infrastructure for Reliable Federated Business Intelligence.

What this is. SARAI is a Design Science Research artefact that federates a PostgreSQL fact store and a MariaDB dimension store behind a single SQL endpoint, adds four proactive reliability mechanisms, and evaluates the resulting decision-support stack against a stratified benchmark of 50 federated questions across five business domains and five complexity tiers. 24 of the 50 questions require a genuine cross-engine join, not two independent reads.

Headline results. 50/50 gold queries execute and satisfy their own programmatic result-set validators in about 60 s. On a matched panel the query-accuracy gap between full-sovereignty local inference and a hosted model is 30 percentage points. The SQL anomaly detector reaches F1 = 0.980 on structural and adversarial injection workloads, with a separate audit against organic model failure cases.

Two halves of reproducibility, kept separate. The analysis half runs anywhere: three scripts regenerate the manuscript's latency statistics, cost model and graded-sovereignty ladder from the one committed benchmark run, and 16 assertions check every value still matches the paper. The data half needs the federated stack, which docker-compose.yml provides using PrestoDB 0.284 — the engine the patent names, not Trino. Both run in continuous integration.

What is deliberately not reproducible, and why. The manuscript's reported accuracies came from hosted models called over HTTP (gemma-3-27b-it:free, llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free, deepseek-r1-0528:free). A free-tier endpoint can change or be withdrawn, so no one can reproduce those numbers without pinning and archiving the exact model versions. Substituting a local model would only demonstrate the harness, while implying something about the paper that is not true. This limitation is stated in REPRODUCIBILITY.md and in the CI workflow header rather than papered over. Latency is likewise hardware-bound and is not asserted.

Data. 371 MB of source tables are not in the archive. They are four public Kaggle datasets and one UCI dataset, published frozen as a separate release asset, sarai-datasets-v1.tar.gz, so the reported row counts are reproducible. A newer revision of a live Kaggle dataset would change those counts and make the validators fail in a way that looks like a code bug.

Licence. CC BY 4.0 for everything this work produced. The five datasets keep their upstream licences (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, CC0-1.0, CC BY 4.0 and DbCL-1.0 respectively) and are not relicensed here.

Scope of this deposit. This record contains the code. The 371 MB of source tables are not included, for two reasons. First, a Zenodo record carries a single licence field while the five upstream sources carry three different licences — CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for the e-commerce and supply-chain sets, CC0-1.0 for the healthcare set, CC BY 4.0 for the UCI retail set and DbCL-1.0 for the fraud set, two of them non-commercial — so one licence line could not describe them accurately. Second, the exact files are already addressable: they are frozen as the datasets-v1 release asset of the repository, and each source keeps its own upstream DOI. REPRODUCIBILITY.md states where each comes from and how to fetch it.
notes: This record is the software artefact for the manuscript "SARAI: Sovereignty-Aware Risk Assessment Infrastructure for Reliable Federated Business Intelligence", which is under review. The DOI above is the permanent, credential-free location for the artefact code. The five public source datasets are not redistributed here, because a single Zenodo record carries one licence while those sources carry three different ones, two of them non-commercial; see LICENSE and REPRODUCIBILITY.md for each source and how to obtain it. The code repository is private while the manuscript is under review, so no repository related-identifier is given here: a link that returns 404 from a permanent record is worse than no link. A related identifier can be added once the repository is public, since Zenodo freezes files on publish but not metadata.
